LeakSanitizer is enabled by default in the Rust ASan build on Linux; the S1 workspace pass therefore exercises leak detection with zero leaks required for exit 0 (same log as ASan)

S2 stage — quickjs-ng sources compiled by the rquickjs-sys cc build with clang -fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all; test binary linked by clang. Rust-side UBSan is not separately run: rustc -Zsanitizer accepts one sanitizer per build and the workspace's release-critical invariants are exercised under ASan S1

fuzz/miri-scope.json — included: q-runtime-model, q-router, q-schema-runtime, q-bridge, q-pack; all others excluded with recorded reasons and compensations; unsafe-audit.py fails closed on a crate missing from the map

The concurrency-critical first-party surface (q-bridge bounded slab, dispatcher fairness/shutdown, worker lifecycle) is exercised by deterministic property suites (q-bridge slab lifecycle/fuzz target, M3-005/M3-008 fairness + shutdown, M3-007 cancellation) and the 24h/72h soak under concurrent producers. Full-workspace TSan is waived for M6-003: tokio/hyper do not compile cleanly under TSan without tokio_unstable cfg churn, and the serving path contains no custom lock-free algorithm where TSan's unique value lies. Revisit trigger: any hand-rolled lock-free structure entering the serving path.

Loom model-checks custom schedulers/lock-free structures; Velqu's scheduler is tokio with bounded channels and generation-checked slots whose interleavings are covered by the deterministic property suites above plus the chaos program (M3-010-B, beta-009-d). No custom lock-free algorithm exists in the serving path. Revisit trigger: same as TSan.
